findings.text: Public extraction entry selects a backing-specific helper based on iterator kind covering user, kvec, bvec, folio queue and xarray cases and signals unsupported kinds with a fault error.
Public helper builds bio vectors from extracted pages with alignment validation, folio contiguity grouping, zone device mapping compatibility handling, and cleanup of surplus pinned pages.
Requested extraction length is bounded above by remaining iterator count and by a global read-write limit, with empty requests completing successfully without touching backing storage.

Kvec extraction ignores fully consumed segments, exposes the offset inside the first page, resolves each covered page through either vmalloc or direct translation, and accounts consumed length in the iterator.

User-backed extraction derives pinning options from destination direction, peer allowance and no-fault mode, pins the addressed range, releases a freshly allocated page array on pin failure, and accounts the pinned length.

Bvec extraction rejects misaligned starts or lengths for simple iterators and misaligned aggregate alignment otherwise, then groups consecutive pages that belong to one folio and are physically adjacent.
The count of page pointers that fit in one bio vector slot determines how page array storage overlays caller bio vector storage during bvec extraction.

If zone device mapping differs or fewer folio-contiguous pages remain, extraction stops early, returns the unconsumed tail to the iterator, releases surplus pinned pages, and reports only the materialized prefix.
Scheduling, completion, disable, enable and initialization routines form the public control surface for interrupt poll instances with configurable weight and callback.
Scheduling is a no-op when disabled or already scheduled; otherwise the instance is queued on the local CPU list and the poll soft interrupt is raised.

An instance cycles between unscheduled, scheduled-queued, and disabled conditions driven by schedule, completion, disable-spin and enable-clear transitions with ordered clearing of the scheduled flag.
Queue and dequeue operations hold local interrupt exclusion, while the soft handler drops exclusion only around the driver callback and relies on append-only tail growth for safe head access.
The poll handler consumes a global budget by completed work and observes a start-time window; exhausting either defers remaining instances by re-raising the soft interrupt.
Instances reporting at least their weight are retained by the handler, moved to the list tail when enabled or completed when disabled, without requiring driver state changes.
Module initialization creates per-CPU lists, registers the poll soft handler, and installs a CPU-dead hook that migrates a departing CPU queue to the current CPU.
Offline migration splices the dead CPU queue under bottom-half and interrupt exclusion and ensures the poll soft interrupt is pending on the surviving CPU.
Default soft handler work budget is 256 units, stored in a read-mostly global.
Poll instance carries a list node, a flag word with scheduled and disabled bits, a weight limit, and a callback invoked with the instance and weight.
Each CPU maintains its own poll queue head and its own saved interrupt register pointer through per-CPU storage.
Predicate reports whether the calling thread is the sole user of its address space after checking thread count, address-space sharing, and a global process scan.

Non-singleton thread groups fail immediately, uniquely referenced address spaces succeed immediately, otherwise kernel threads and the caller group leader are ignored while scanning for another user of the same address space.
The scan combines atomic counters for liveness and sharing with read-side RCU exclusion and an ordering barrier when encountering a thread with a temporarily empty address-space pointer.
Formatting helper avoids general formatting work for literal formats and for a lone string directive by duplicating the constant or argument directly, falling back to general formatting otherwise.
FIFO state holds monotonically increasing input and output counters, a size mask, element size, and backing buffer pointer, with occupancy defined as input minus output and capacity as mask plus one.
Allocation, initialization from caller storage, and release manage the FIFO control block, enforcing power-of-two capacity and a minimum of two elements.
Allocation rounds requested element counts up to a power of two while initialization from existing storage rounds non-power-of-two sizes down after accounting for element size.
Input is limited by free slots and output or peek by occupied slots, with linear output additionally limited by distance to the end of the backing buffer.
Copies split at the buffer wrap boundary into at most two segments and order data visibility before the corresponding counter update with a write barrier.
User-copy and scatterlist preparation variants expose FIFO contents across privilege and DMA boundaries, reporting copied element counts and fault status or prepared segment counts.
User-copy helpers convert residual byte counts into whole-element deficits, advance counters only by fully transferred elements, and signal partial transfers with a fault status.

DMA preparation clamps length to available free or occupied space and describes the region with one entry when contiguous or two entries when wrapping, optionally filling device addresses when mapping succeeded.
Record mode prefixes each payload with a one or two byte length header, caps payloads to the maximum encodable by the header width, and rejects enqueue when header plus payload does not fit.

Record peek leaves counters unchanged, dequeue and user dequeue consume the full stored record even when the caller buffer is smaller, skip discards a whole record, and empty queues report zero length.
Record receive from user and DMA preparation validate whole-record fit before touching state, and DMA finish writes the header and advances past header plus payload in one step.

Index arithmetic relies on unsigned wrap and power-of-two masking, DMA record preparation requires at least one scatterlist slot, and callers must serialize concurrent writers or readers beyond the barriers shown.
Producers and consumers publish copied data with a write barrier before updating input or output counters, without taking a lock in these helpers.
